Fresh review of the current query_value claim and all current evidence, using the recorded CI coordinator instructions. The one ordinary implementation entry is Stashed::new in crates/sage-stash/src/lib.rs; its current preview also includes the signature.storage association. Inspected the whole captured implementation file, including current owned_products/signature.storage markers at the constructor, fingerprint traversal, storage helpers, handle definitions, equality and Update. The complete associated test set is one ordinary incremental test. No TODO/N/A entries require justification.

The claim has four aspects: a tree is one incremental value; Salsa compares and backdates its Stashed root as a unit; its internal nodes are not independently tracked identities; and finer boundaries are external semantic queries rather than internal handles. Stashed owns the arena, root and fingerprint together. Construction computes a root-reachable fingerprint. FingerprintHasher traverses Ptr and Slice contents and hashes slice length/order; entry indices are cache keys, not the value fingerprint. Equality compares the single root fingerprint. With the salsa feature, Stashed::maybe_update returns false and retains the old complete tree when equal, and replaces the whole value when different. Ptr/Slice are ordinary local index handles with no tracked identity or database ingredient. Their own Update implementations compare indices but do not register tracked nodes; ordinary stash indexing has no database dependency reads. The public reflection index is explicitly within-stash and not a cross-revision semantic identity. The additional constructor associations do not alter these behaviors. Essential production helpers are all in the associated implementation file.

Captured the entire incremental.rs through review read to inspect the producer, consumer, database and input helpers. produce returns Stashed<Slice<Ptr<u32>>> from ordinary node allocations, and consume is a separate tracked scalar semantic query over that tree. The annotated test directly asserts initial result 21 with consume/produce execution; warm demand with no execution; a layout-only edit causing no eager execution then produce-only execution and unchanged result; a reachable value edit causing result 41 and produce/consume execution; and an unrelated input edit causing neither execution nor result change. The producer layout variant adds unreachable data and reverses child allocation order, making the equal-root assertion meaningful despite changed handles. Thus comparison by handle/layout would fail the backdating assertion, and always returning unchanged would fail the reachable-content result and execution assertion. The absence of independent node tracking is supported by direct structural inspection as well as this root/query separation. Meaningful expected values and execution assertions are visible in the test body rather than hidden in a verification wrapper.

All claim aspects are accounted for by current source and test assertions; no changes requested. This refresh is a source review, not a new test run: the coordinator runs suites centrally. The incremental test file requires the salsa feature. Executed review start and dependency reads, and submit through review record; no Rust or specification files were modified. The assessment does not rely on the earlier approval or claim that its prior test execution validates this refreshed state.
